question: Should the staged authorization, credential-free execution and validation, strict base binding, and receipt-bound mutation design at 84e4c6ed31a8b1d120f99344756676eeca62af80 replace the current production repair security boundary?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent, but it intentionally changes credential possession, proof authority, repository protection requirements, mutation ordering, failure recovery, and operational topology; accepting and rolling out that production trust model requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve after canary
options.body: Wait for all exact-head checks, verify production token and ruleset configuration, and run one controlled end-to-end repair before enabling the new path broadly.

options.title: Split the rollout
options.body: Land deterministic staged proof separately while deferring privileged publication and strict-base enforcement to a smaller independently canaried change.

options.title: Pause the redesign
options.body: Retain the current workflow if maintainers do not want to own the new configuration requirements and operational failure modes.

recommendation.title: Approve after canary
recommendation.body: Wait for all exact-head checks, verify production token and ruleset configuration, and run one controlled end-to-end repair before enabling the new path broadly.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main provenance and the branch history place vincentkoc at the center of the repair execution and publication boundary being redesigned.
